item.title: SenseNova-Loop-9B
item.content:encoded:
You need to agree to share your Hugging Face information to access this model

This repository is publicly accessible, but you have to accept the conditions to access its files and content.

Log in or Sign Up to review the conditions and access this model content.

SenseNova-Loop-9B

English | 简体中文

🌐 Architecture

📣 News

🔥 2026-11-18: Added download links for the AWQ and GGUF weights.

🔥 2026-11-17: We release SenseNova-Loop-9B, with model weights and code available to the community.

🔥 2026-10-31: We release SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview, with model weights and code available to the community.

🚀 SenseNova-Loop-9B: Deeper Computation with Fewer Parameters

We officially release SenseNova-Loop-9B. Building on the Preview's exploration of parameter efficiency, the model reuses layer weights through a looped architecture and combines them with manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) to expand computational depth within a compact parameter budget. It is designed for complex reasoning, coding, tool use, and multimodal tasks.

Since the Preview release, we have received community interest and feedback on model use, inference deployment, and ecosystem integration. The official release retains the looped architecture and two-stream mHC, further improving performance on agentic, coding, and data analysis tasks while continuing to explore the capabilities of looped computation.

SenseNova-Loop-9B has approximately 9B parameters. By repeatedly executing shared middle layers, it extends 32 physical decoder layers into 56 layer executions. The model accepts text and images and generates text, supporting long-context understanding and multi-step tasks. In agentic and data analysis evaluations, the model is competitive with Qwen3.8-27B: it scores 41.36 versus 44.60 on NL2Repo and 65.31 versus 65.01 on AIDABench.

Model Highlights

  • Shared looped block: 24 decoder layers are executed twice in sequence, producing 56 layer computations from 32 distinct layers per forward pass.
  • Two-stream mHC: learned mappings route and combine information between two residual streams within the looped block.
  • Hybrid attention: the decoder interleaves linear and full attention in a repeating four-layer pattern.
  • Long-context multimodal training: the training recipe includes text, images, code, and tool-use trajectories, with the context length extended to 512K tokens.
  • Low-memory deployment: With 4-bit weights and an 8-bit KV cache, multimodal inference at a 256K context length requires approximately 15 GiB of GPU memory.
  • Official quantized release: An official AWQ 4-bit version is available on launch day for easier deployment.

🎬 Showcase

3D

SVG + Web

Poster

Web

Design

📊 Model Performance: From Preview to Release

We evaluate SenseNova-Loop-9B on agentic, coding, and data analysis tasks, comparing the release with the Preview and other models.

The release outperforms the Preview on all seven benchmarks shown. AutomationBench rises from 14.33 to 36.67, Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 40.45 to 59.55, and GAIA from 37.86 to 69.90.

Compared with Qwen3.8-27B, the release matches its 36.67 on AutomationBench and scores 65.31 versus 65.01 on AIDABench. On NL2Repo, it scores 41.36 versus 44.60. Its BIRD score of 72.34 is 0.96 percentage points above the Preview's 71.38.

🧠 Model Architecture

SenseNova-Loop-9B is built on a 32-layer multimodal decoder combining shared-weight looped computation, hybrid attention, and two-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC). It extends computation depth by reusing middle-layer parameters, accepts text and images, generates text, and supports a context length of up to 512K tokens.

Model Specifications

PropertySenseNova-Loop-9B
ArchitectureAutoregressive multimodal decoder; looped block with two-stream mHC
Parameter scaleApproximately 9B total parameters; approximately 14.6B inference-equivalent parameters
Input / outputText and images / text
Distinct decoder layers32
Looped layer range / passes[4, 28) / 2, with shared weights
Decoder layer executions56 per forward pass
mHC residual streams2
Context length512K tokens
Weight precisionBF16 backbone; FP32 mHC routing parameters

Looped Decoder

Inputs first pass through layers 0–3, then through the same block of layers 4–27 twice, and finally through layers 28–31 and the output head. If B denotes the looped block and h its input, the looped computation can be written as B(B(h)).

During inference, each forward pass performs 56 decoder-layer computations while storing only 32 sets of decoder-layer weights. The looped block shares the same weights across both passes, with the output of the first pass serving as input to the second.

Hybrid Attention

The decoder interleaves linear attention and full attention. Each group of four layers contains three linear-attention layers followed by one full-attention layer. The loop boundaries align with complete four-layer groups, so both passes preserve the same attention pattern.

Two-Stream mHC

Within the looped block, mHC uses two residual streams to carry information around decoder-layer computations. Learned mappings determine how each layer reads from the streams, mixes information between them, and writes its output back to the residual state. The stream-mixing map is constrained with Sinkhorn normalization, using 20 iterations in the model configuration.

The two streams can be viewed as two sets of hidden states carried in parallel. A looped layer reads from the streams, applies attention or feed-forward computation, and writes its output back. Repeated row and column normalization constrains how information is mixed between the streams. These 20 normalization iterations are internal to mHC and are separate from the two passes through the looped block.

The loop range, number of passes, and mHC routing parameters together define the checkpoint's execution configuration. A compatible inference implementation must load these parameters and preserve the same computation order.

ConfigurationValue
Distinct decoder layers / executions32 / 56
Looped layer range / passes[4, 28) / 2
Hidden dimension4,096
Feed-forward dimension12,288
Vocabulary size248,320
Full-attention heads / KV heads16 / 4
mHC residual streams / Sinkhorn iterations2 / 20

🔬 Loop Scaling: Exploring the Benefits of Looped Computation

Looped Transformers show promising performance scaling, offering another way to expand model capability through repeated computation. Using the original 9B model with a standard single forward pass (Loop 1) as the baseline, we vary the number of loops while holding the training data and other settings constant. Overall performance improves across the four tasks, with the best results at three or four loops. AIDABench-QA and Workbuddy-office peak at three loops, improving by 6.42% and 16.93% relative to the baseline; LiveCodeBench V6 and AIDABench data visualization peak at four loops, improving by 8.10% and 8.55%.

To balance inference efficiency, both the Preview and the release use two loops by default. Deeper loops nevertheless provide further gains: moving from two to four loops improves LiveCodeBench V6 by 1.04 percentage points and AIDABench data visualization by 1.35 percentage points. These experiments cover one to four loops, leaving the potential of deeper looping open for further study.

Different tasks respond differently to loop depth. We will continue exploring deeper computation and Dynamic Loop architectures that adapt the number of loops to each input, allocating computation according to task complexity.

💾 Low-Memory Deployment

The shared looped architecture uses approximately 9B distinct parameters. With 4-bit weight quantization, the model weights occupy approximately 4.9 GB. Using an 8-bit or 4-bit KV cache can further reduce memory requirements for long-context inference. The estimated minimum GPU memory requirements for deployment are:

Context length8-bit KV cache4-bit KV cache
64K~10 GiB~9 GiB
128K~12 GiB~10 GiB
256K~15 GiB~12 GiB

Get Started

Model Weights

WeightsDownloadFiles
BF16Hugging Face · ModelScopeRelease weights in Safetensors format
AWQHugging Face4-bit AWQ weights and matching MTP draft
GGUFHugging FaceBF16, Q8_0, Q5_K_M, and Q4_K_M

Text Generation with Transformers

Use Transformers to load the model from a Hugging Face repository or a local model directory. The examples below cover single-GPU text generation and serving with inference engines.

Requirements

The checked Preview environment uses Transformers 5.18.0, PyTorch 2.11.0, and CUDA 13.0. The model directory must include the configuration, tokenizer, chat template, custom model code, and all weight shards.

First install a CUDA-compatible build of PyTorch, then install the remaining dependencies:

python -m pip install "transformers==5.18.0" accelerate safetensors

Set model_id to the release model directory or repository ID, then run:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model_id = "/path/to/SenseNova-Loop-9B"
device = "cuda:0"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map={"": device},
).eval()

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 13 times 7?"}]
prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=False,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    enable_thinking=True,
)
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model.generate(
        **inputs,
        max_new_tokens=512,
        do_sample=False,
        use_cache=True,
    )
response = tokenizer.decode(
    outputs[0, inputs.input_ids.shape[1]:],
    skip_special_tokens=True,
)
print(response)

The example enables thinking mode, uses greedy decoding, and generates up to 512 new tokens. Set enable_thinking to False to disable thinking, or change device to select a GPU. trust_remote_code=True loads the custom SenseNova Loop model implementation.

Deployment

The following commands are adapted from the Preview deployment examples. Replace the model path with the release checkpoint directory; the release engine versions and configurations will be updated with the model.

LightLLM

Four-GPU deployment example:

docker pull ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main

docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /path/to/SenseNova-Loop-9B:/model \
  -e LOADWORKER=4 -e LIGHTLLM_TRITON_AUTOTUNE_LEVEL=1 \
  ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main \
  python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /model --model_name SenseNova-Loop-9B \
    --tp 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

Once the service is running, send an OpenAI-compatible request:

curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "SenseNova-Loop-9B", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], "max_tokens": 128}'

SGLang

Use the version from SGLang PR #47281, which includes the SenseNova Loop implementation, and replace the model path:

git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git
cd sglang
git fetch origin pull/47281/head
git checkout -b sensenova-loop FETCH_HEAD
python -m pip install -e ./python

sglang serve --model-path /path/to/SenseNova-Loop-9B

vLLM

For text generation, build vLLM from the SenseNova Loop branch in vLLM PR #64832, which supports the published AWQ checkpoint.

git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
cd vllm
git fetch origin pull/64832/head
git checkout -b sensenova-loop FETCH_HEAD
python -m pip install -e .

To serve the BF16 checkpoint:

vllm serve sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B \
  --served-model-name sensenova_loop \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --dtype bfloat16

To serve the 4-bit AWQ checkpoint on a single GPU:

vllm serve sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B-AWQ \
  --served-model-name sensenova_loop \
  --dtype bfloat16

vLLM detects AWQ from the checkpoint configuration.

Inference Acceleration

SenseNova-Loop supports MTP speculative decoding. DSpark and DFlash2 draft model training instructions are available in SenseSpec; available release draft weights and launch settings will be updated with the model.

🏋️ Training

For model fine-tuning, refer to the SenseNova-Loop examples in OpenSenseNova/torchtitan.

Training scripts for DSpark and DFlash2 speculative decoding draft models are available in OpenSenseNova/SenseSpec.

⚠️ Known Limitations

Given its size and development time, SenseNova-Loop-9B has room for improvement in the following areas:

  • Complex instruction following: The model may misunderstand or miss requirements when given many complex tool definitions or multiple constraints.
  • Coding and general agent tasks: Performance can be inconsistent on coding and general agent tasks. The model can correct some errors through additional steps, but its ability to handle complex, long-horizon tasks still needs improvement.
  • Complex web generation: Websites with complex 3D scenes and rich animations may not be completed in a single turn. Some examples require user feedback and two to three rounds of refinement.

We will continue to improve the model and plan to apply the Loop architecture to larger models in the future. We welcome community feedback and reports of issues.

📄 License and Citation

The model project is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

item.title: SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-TailSteer
item.content:encoded:
SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT · TailSteer

Edit images in your browser — no local setup needed. Community demo by hugging-apps (Poli).

Join the TailSteer Adventure! ✨

We'd love to see what you create with TailSteer! Share your results, ideas, or feedback with us—every little creation makes our day! (≧▽≦) ♡

If you'd like to support our work, a ⭐ on GitHub or a ❤️ on Hugging Face would mean a lot—and stay tuned to our GitHub repo for future TailSteer-trained model releases! (ง •̀ᴗ•́)ง ♡

Keep creating. Keep the details.

Preserve the generation and editing strengths of SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT. Unlock greater stability across repeated edits. TailSteer is a final training stage that largely retains the base model's learned capabilities while reducing the drift that builds up when each edit becomes the next input.

Try the model · Single-turn results · Add & Preserve · Training data

+6.99 dB PSNR · 31.3% lower LPIPS outside the edit region at turn 10 on Add & Preserve.

Keep building the scene. Keep its structure.

Twenty instructions transform an elevated railway scene. TailSteer keeps the train, tracks and city legible as the base model accumulates texture artifacts. Each branch feeds its own previous output into the next turn. View the final comparison · Prompts and frames.

Use your existing pipeline

Same architecture. Same official model layout. Same loading API. These are complete model weights: replace your original model ID or local path with sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-TailSteer. No adapters, merging, extra inference modules or TailSteer-specific runtime are required.

Use the same official environment as the base model. Only the model ID changes.

With the official SenseNova inference package:

python examples/editing/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-TailSteer \
  --image input.png --prompt "Change the jacket to blue." --output output.png

For the next edit, pass the edited image back into the same pipeline. Use TailSteer throughout the original denoising trajectory; no model switching or preservation mask is needed at inference.

Keep the foundation model's strengths

Same prompt and seed in each pair. Full prompts and images.

The same checkpoint supports text-to-image generation and single-turn editing. Across Qwen-Image-Bench, BizGenEval, GEdit and ImgEdit, scores stay close to the base model. The table includes RISE as well, where accuracy is lower in this setting.

BenchmarkBase modelAfter TailSteer
Qwen-IB EN ↑53.4352.24
Qwen-IB ZH ↑53.2552.58
BizGen ES (%) ↑45.8545.73
GEdit EN ↑8.338.27
GEdit ZH ↑8.308.31
RISE accuracy (%) ↑31.3929.44
ImgEdit ↑4.434.41

Compose objects without rebuilding the scene

The same editor also accepts multiple reference images. Here, successive objects are introduced into an atrium while TailSteer better preserves the evolving scene. View the final comparison.

Measure what stays unchanged

Add & Preserve makes drift visible: add a small object inside the red box at each turn, retain previous objects, and preserve everything outside. It tests both object completion and background preservation across 100 images and ten turns.

ModelCOA (%) ↑PSNR@10 ↑SSIM@10 ↑LPIPS@10 ↓
Base model94.9311.230.1660.607
After TailSteer94.7818.220.4890.417

COA (Cumulative Object Accuracy) averages requested-object presence across ten turns. PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS measure the unchanged region. These are standard image-feedback results; curves use all 100 images. Metric data.

Run demos and benchmarks

With the TailSteer codebase installed in the official backbone environment:

tailsteer infer --backbone sensenova-u1.5-8b-mot \
  --checkpoint sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-TailSteer \
  --policies tailsteer --inference-suite cafe-20turn --gpus 1

Prepare the original base weights and omit --policies tailsteer for side-by-side comparisons. The same suite interface runs text-to-image, single-turn editing, multi-turn editing and Add & Preserve benchmarks after their datasets and judges are configured.

→ Explore and learn why TailSteer works

Preserve early dynamics; steer the trajectory tail. TailSteer learns from the editor's own denoising rollouts, using unchanged source content as a preservation reference. It improves long-horizon stability using single-edit trajectories, without requiring curated ground-truth editing pairs or training on multi-turn editing chains.

This is the paper's 2,000-update checkpoint, with training steering onset 42 / 50. The onset controls training supervision; inference uses the trained model at every step. The packaged model was validated against the original inference export.

From TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing.

item.title: SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview
item.content:encoded:
SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview

English | 简体中文

📣 News

  • [2026.10.30] We release SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview, a looped multimodal model for long-context and agentic workflows.

🚀 SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview

🎬 Showcase (Created by Raccoon Work)

Motion Design

PPT Design

Data Analysis

Overview

SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview is a multimodal language model developed for long-context and agentic workflows. It accepts text and images and generates text for applications that combine document understanding, coding, and interaction with external tools.

The model combines a looped decoder with two-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC). A contiguous block of decoder layers is executed twice with shared weights, while learned mappings manage information flow between two residual streams in the looped section. Together, these components provide a deeper execution path without duplicating the repeated block's parameters.

Documented training recipes combine long sequences, multimodal inputs, and supervised task trajectories, with a maximum training sequence length of 262,144 tokens. For the best model performance, we recommend using our documented deployment environment and configuration parameters.

Model highlights

  • Shared looped block: 24 decoder layers are applied twice in sequence, producing 56 decoder-layer executions from 32 distinct layers.
  • Two-stream mHC: learned mappings route and combine information across two residual streams in the looped section.
  • Hybrid attention: the decoder interleaves linear and full attention in a repeating four-layer pattern.
  • Long-context multimodal training: documented recipes include text, images, code, and tool trajectories at sequence lengths up to 256K tokens.

📊 Key Benchmarks

Model specifications

PropertySenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview
ArchitectureAutoregressive multimodal decoder; looped block with two-stream mHC
Backbone scale~9B total parameters; ~14.6B inference parameters
Input / outputText and images / text
Distinct decoder layers32
Looped layers / passes[4, 28) / 2, with shared weights
Decoder layer executions56 per forward pass
mHC streams2
Training contextUp to 262,144 tokens
Existing export precisionBF16 backbone; FP32 mHC routing parameters

Model architecture

SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview builds on a 32-layer multimodal decoder that combines shared-weight looped computation, hybrid attention, and two-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC). The following sections describe how these components extend the computation path and manage information flow through the model.

Looped decoder

The decoder first processes the input through layers 0–3. The same block of layers 4–27 is then applied twice in sequence, after which layers 28–31 and the output head produce the model's output. If B represents the repeated block and h its input, the looped computation can be written as B(B(h)).

During inference, the model performs 56 decoder-layer computations per forward pass while storing only 32 sets of decoder-layer weights. The looped block reuses the same weights across both passes, with the second pass taking the first pass's output as input.

Hybrid attention

The decoder interleaves linear-attention and full-attention layers. Each four-layer group contains three linear-attention layers followed by one full-attention layer. The loop boundaries align with complete four-layer groups, so the attention pattern is preserved across both passes.

Two-stream mHC

Inside the looped section, mHC carries two residual streams around the decoder-layer computations. Learned mappings govern how a layer reads from the streams, mixes stream information, and incorporates the layer output into the residual state. Sinkhorn normalization constrains the stream-mixing map; the documented configuration uses 20 iterations.

The loop range, pass count, and mHC routing parameters form part of the checkpoint's execution configuration. A compatible inference implementation must load these parameters and reproduce the same execution order.

ConfigurationValue
Distinct decoder layers / executions32 / 56
Repeated block / passes[4, 28) / 2
Hidden dimension4,096
Feed-forward dimension12,288
Vocabulary size248,320
Full-attention heads / KV heads16 / 4
mHC streams / Sinkhorn iterations2 / 20

Inference acceleration

SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview supports MTP for accelerated inference. Dspark and Dflash2 are under development, with training currently in progress.

MethodStatus
MTPAvailable
DsparkTraining in progress
Dflash2Training in progress

Practical speedups depend on the workload, hardware, and serving configuration.

Models and resources

ResourceStatus
Model weightsHugging Face model page
Transformers inference implementationPublication details to be announced
Technical reportTBD

Getting started

Use Transformers to load the model and its custom implementation from a Hugging Face repository or a local model directory. The example below runs text generation on a single GPU.

Requirements

The checked inference environment uses Transformers 5.18.0 and PyTorch 2.11.0 with CUDA 13.0. The model directory must include the configuration, tokenizer, chat template, model code, and accessible weight shards.

First install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA environment, then install the remaining dependencies:

python -m pip install "transformers==5.18.0" accelerate safetensors

Text generation with Transformers

Set model_id to the Hugging Face repository ID or a local model directory, then run:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model_id = "sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview"
device = "cuda:0"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map={"": device},
).eval()

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 13 times 7? Reply with the number only."}]
prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=False,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    enable_thinking=False,
)
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(device)

with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model.generate(
        **inputs,
        max_new_tokens=256,
        do_sample=False,
        use_cache=True,
    )

response = tokenizer.decode(
    outputs[0, inputs.input_ids.shape[1]:],
    skip_special_tokens=True,
)
print(response)

The example uses greedy decoding and generates up to 256 new tokens. Set enable_thinking=True to enable thinking mode, or change device to select another GPU.

trust_remote_code=True loads the custom SenseNova Loop model implementation.

Training

Model training

To fine-tune SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview with mHC on a single node with 8 GPUs, run the following commands in your configured training environment:

git clone https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/torchtitan.git
cd torchtitan
MODEL_PATH=/path/to/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview DATASET=/path/to/train.jsonl \
  bash examples/train/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview/mhc2_loop2_titan.sh

Replace /path/to/train.jsonl with your SFT dataset. See the training guide for configuration options, DPO, and MTP training.

Speculative Decoding Training

To train a DSpark or DFlash2 draft model for SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview on a single node with 8 GPUs, use the training scripts provided in the SenseSpec repository.

First, clone the repository and navigate to the project directory:

git clone https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseSpec.git
cd SenseSpec

DSpark Training

Run the following command to train the DSpark draft model:

bash examples/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview-dspark/run.sh

DFlash2 Training

Run the following command to train the DFlash2 draft model:

bash examples/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview-dflash2/run.sh

Deployment

LightLLM

Four-GPU example; replace the local model path:

docker pull ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main

docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /path/to/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview:/model \
  -e LOADWORKER=4 -e LIGHTLLM_TRITON_AUTOTUNE_LEVEL=1 \
  ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main \
  python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /model --model_name SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview \
    --tp 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

Example request:

curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], "max_tokens": 128}'

SGLang

Use the version from SGLang PR #47281, which includes the SenseNova Loop implementation, and replace the model path below with your local checkpoint directory:

git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git
cd sglang
git fetch origin pull/47281/head
git checkout -b sensenova-loop FETCH_HEAD
python -m pip install -e ./python

sglang serve --model-path /path/to/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview

vLLM

Use the version from vLLM PR #64832, which includes the SenseNova Loop implementation, for inference:

git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
cd vllm
git fetch origin pull/64832/head
git checkout -b sensenova-loop FETCH_HEAD
python -m pip install -e .

vllm serve sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview \
  --served-model-name sensenova_loop \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --dtype bfloat16

License and citation

License: Apache License 2.0. Citation:

@misc{sensenova2026loop,
  title        = {{SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview}},

item.title: SenseNova-6.8-Code2Video
item.content:encoded:
SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video

A code-driven video creation model, fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B

Launch film (90 s, with sound), made by SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video

We present SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video, a lightweight open model for code-driven video creation. The model builds and renders videos by generating executable code, and currently focuses on short videos implemented entirely in code. Preliminary results show good visual composition and motion choreography in motion design, suggesting the potential of lightweight models for programmatic video creation.

We chose code as the entry point to video creation partly for its ability to connect different models and creative tools. Beyond building and rendering visual content directly, code can call image generation, video generation, 3D modelling and video editing models and tools, chaining generation, editing and compositing into a complete creative workflow.

We believe code can become a common language between ideas and finished work. Our long-term goal is a model that coordinates different generative models and creative tools through code to create digital content across media. SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video is a first step in this direction. Next, we will scale the model further and extend these abilities to editing, compositing, animation and 3D content creation.

Released Resources

ResourceLocationDescription
Model weightsThis repositoryWeights, config and tokenizer
Example trajectoriestrajectories/Message and tool logs with figures
Production skillGitHubWorkflow, craft guides, rendering tools

Deployment

LightLLM

docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /path/to/SenseNova-6.8-Code2Video:/model \
  ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main \
  python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /model \
    --tp 4 \
    --max_req_total_len 524288 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

vLLM

docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -e VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 \
  -v /path/to/SenseNova-6.8-Code2Video:/model \
  vllm/vllm-openai:latest \
    --model /model \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --max-model-len 524288 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

SGLang

docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -e SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 \
  -v /path/to/SenseNova-6.8-Code2Video:/model \
  lmsysorg/sglang:latest \
  python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /model \
    --tp-size 4 \
    --context-length 524288 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

Recommended harness: Claude Code

A complete film is a long-horizon task: the model writes and renders code, reviews the frames and revises, turn after turn. SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video sustains runs of more than 10 hours and more than 2,000 turns. Configure Claude Code for runs of that length:

SettingValueConfiguration
Context window512KCLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=524288
Auto-compaction0.8CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=80
Max output64KCLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=64000
Turns per run2,000+--max-turns 2000 or more
Time per run10 h+timeout 10h or more

Set the context window explicitly, since Claude Code otherwise treats an unknown model as a 200K model. With compaction at 0.8 and 64K of output, every request stays within the 512K server limit.

Put the endpoint and these variables in a private settings file, and supply the credential through ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://your-endpoint.example.com",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "your-deployed-model-name",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS": "524288",
    "CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE": "80",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS": "64000"
  },
  "model": "your-deployed-model-name"
}

Avoid slow shell initialization: every Bash call starts a new shell.

Usage

Producing a film has three stages:

StagePerformed byOutput
1. Prompt enhancementA strong general model (we use Claude Opus 5.5) with the Enhance prompt templatedense_prompt.md
2. ProductionSenseNova 6.8 Code2Video in Claude Code with the code-video skillout/final.mp4, SPEC.md, VERIFY.md
3. Revision (optional)The creator writes notes; SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video applies them in the same projectA new version of the film

Stage 2 with the settings above:

cd /path/to/task   # contains dense_prompt.md, assets/ and .claude/skills/code-video
claude -p --settings /path/to/private-settings.json --model your-deployed-model-name \
  --max-turns 2000 --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Skill" \
  'Use the project code-video skill. Read .claude/skills/code-video/SKILL.md and dense_prompt.md, then the relevant craft guides. Produce the complete video and deliver out/final.mp4, SPEC.md and VERIFY.md.'

The run executes shell commands without asking, so start it in an isolated working environment. For a revision, run claude -p --continue in the same folder with the creator's notes as the prompt.

Copy the skill into .claude/skills/code-video unchanged and put task-specific requirements in the prompt. Setup steps and dependencies are in the GitHub repository.

Production trajectories

trajectories/all.openai.jsonl holds one film per line, in OpenAI messages format.

Each line contains messages, tools, images, enable_thinking and metadata. The messages include reasoning, tool calls and results, retries and compaction summaries. Images appear as <image> placeholders; the ordered images array gives their paths relative to trajectories/, and all 357 figures are in trajectories/figures/. Private paths and hosts are anonymized, so recorded commands are not directly replayable.

License

Released under the Apache License 2.0.

Contributors

We thank the following contributors for their work on SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video:

  • moolean0
  • sysssyssy
  • TTTTTony
  • craigwu
  • dder4567
  • M1M1cooL
  • egugu
  • luotto

Community Quantizations

We thank the community researchers and contributors below for creating and sharing quantized versions of SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video. Their work makes the model more accessible across a wider range of hardware and helps the community experiment with code-driven video creation.

item.title: SenseNova-RoboRSI-27B-Preview
item.content:encoded:
SenseNova-RoboRSI-27B-Preview

简体中文 · GitHub · Demos · Quickstart

SenseNova-RoboRSI-27B-Preview is an open-weight 27B vision-language model for embodied agents. Through joint model–Harness RSI, it learns from validated interaction experience, developing capabilities for planning, action decisions, and feedback-based correction in simulation and on real robots.

This guide covers model deployment and benchmark reproduction on LIBERO-Pro and RoboCasa365 using RoboRSI Harness. RoboDojo reproduction instructions will be released alongside upcoming RoboDojo support in RoboRSI. A detailed technical report is coming soon.

  • RoboDojo: Achieves an average score of 26.13 and a task success rate of 20.83% with VLA-assisted execution. Its average score is just 2.84 points below GPT-6 Astra's score in the RoboDojo team's evaluation. The model actively inspects visual details, reasons about spatial relationships, and corrects actions based on execution feedback during complex manipulation tasks.
  • LIBERO-Pro: Reaches 92.5% success with VLA-assisted execution (System 2 + System 1) and 95.0% with direct VLM control (System 2), ranking second to GPT-6 Astra among the compared models in both settings. These results demonstrate embodied planning and decision-making across different execution architectures.
  • RoboCasa365: RSI training raises success from 26.0% to 46.5% over the Qwen3.8-27B base model, while reducing average output tokens from 59.5K to 15.9K, a 73.3% reduction. Learning from interaction experience improves both task performance and inference efficiency.

Demonstrations

Real-robot demonstration

Simulation · RoboDojo

Simulation · LIBERO

Simulation · RoboCasa365

Quickstart

1. Deploy the model

Install vLLM

In your inference environment, install the CUDA 12.9 build with a compatible NVIDIA driver:

pip install "vllm==0.21.0" huggingface_hub \
  --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129

See the vLLM installation guide for other CUDA builds.

Download the model

Download the full checkpoint, including the tokenizer, processor, generation configuration, and chat template:

export MODEL_DIR="$PWD/models/sensenova-roborsi-27b-preview"
hf download sensenova/sensenova-roborsi-27b-preview \
  --local-dir "$MODEL_DIR"

For an existing local checkpoint, set MODEL_DIR to its absolute path.

Start the service

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3

vllm serve "$MODEL_DIR" \
  --served-model-name sensenova-roborsi-27b-preview \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --generation-config auto \
  --chat-template "$MODEL_DIR/chat_template.jinja" \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar","disable_any_whitespace":true}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align

We recommend medium reasoning effort for this preview. Set chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort explicitly in vLLM Chat Completions requests, as shown below. The bundled chat template defaults to xhigh when this setting is omitted.

Check the endpoint

From another terminal on the same machine, check service health and send a short robot-planning request:

curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "sensenova-roborsi-27b-preview",
    "messages": [{
      "role": "user",
      "content": "A robot needs to place a mug on a coaster. Give a short plan and explain how to verify that the mug is stable before releasing it."
    }],
    "max_tokens": 8192,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "medium"},
    "stream": false
  }'

2. Connect RoboRSI Harness and run evaluations

Install RoboRSI Harness and the evaluation environment following the model evaluation guide, then use the commands below:

export OPENAI_BASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1'
export OPENAI_API_KEY='EMPTY'
export MODEL_NAME='sensenova-roborsi-27b-preview'

# LIBERO-Pro: VLM + VLA (System 2 + System 1)
# Set up the tool environment, download weights, and deploy VLA/SAM3 in the background; no automatic evaluation
python scripts/deploy/libero_tools.py serve \
  --model-config configs/models/roborsi_27b.yaml \
  --work-dir work/model_eval/libero_tools &

# Wait for Services ready before running the evaluation command below (default URLs shown)
ROBORSI_VLA_URL=http://host.docker.internal:24001 \
ROBORSI_SAM3_URL=http://host.docker.internal:24002 \
python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_model.py --benchmark libero_pro \
  --benchmark-config configs/benchmarks/libero_pro_80.yaml \
  --model-config configs/models/roborsi_27b.yaml \
  --agent-config configs/agents/libero/sensenova_roborsi_27b_vla_sam3.yaml

# LIBERO-Pro: Direct VLM control (System 2); skip the VLA/SAM3 deployment command above
python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_model.py --benchmark libero_pro \
  --benchmark-config configs/benchmarks/libero_pro_80.yaml \
  --model-config configs/models/roborsi_27b.yaml \
  --agent-config configs/agents/libero/sensenova_roborsi_27b_no_tools.yaml

# RoboCasa365
python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_model.py --benchmark robocasa365

# RoboDojo: Evaluation support will be available in a future RoboRSI Harness update

Built on the RoboRSI Harness

SenseNova-RoboRSI-27B-Preview runs within the RoboRSI Harness, the shared foundation for task execution, evaluation, and iterative improvement. This connects the model's learned capabilities to robot actions and turns new interactions into evidence for the next RSI round.

  • Composable execution. Connect models, prompts, skills, and tools/MCP; coordinate VLA skills, scripted actions, or end-effector control through a common agent loop.
  • Reproducible evaluation. Benchmark adapters preserve native execution and scoring, while configurable context, caching, and batch execution support repeatable experiments across environments.
  • Experience for continued learning. Full traces and exported training episodes connect execution to model training; versioned retesting identifies which Harness changes to carry forward.

We develop and maintain SenseNova-RoboRSI on GitHub as the shared foundation for community deployment, reproduction, and continued training. Follow the repository for the Harness, evaluation data, intermediate results, and release updates.

Contributors

  • Project leads: Hanming Deng, Zhongang Cai, Haiwen Diao, Zhi Hou, Zhonghua Wu, Qingyi Tao
  • Model team: Silei Wu*, Weiye Xu, Bo Liu, Pengfei Liu, Tailai Chen, Chenjing Ding, Jiahao Wang, Changxu Wei, Zongpu Zhang
  • Harness team: Jiapeng Luo*, Yuyao Shao, Linjun Dai, Quanzhou Li, Ziyi Shang, Wanqi Yin, Xiaowan Li, Donghao Wu, Tianbo Zhong
  • Advisor: Dahua Lin, Xiaogang Wang, Ziwei Liu, Lewei Lu, Lei Yang
  • denotes team leads.

License

The model weights and model card are released under the Apache License 2.0. See LICENSE for the full license and NOTICE for upstream attribution and a summary of our modifications.

The model is derived from Qwen3.8-27B, whose weights were further post-trained by SenseNova for embodied reasoning and interaction. The upstream license and copyright notice are retained in LICENSE.

External models, simulators, and datasets retain their respective licenses.

item.title: Looped-DiT-B32
item.content:encoded:
Looped-DiT B/32

Looped-DiT is a text-to-image diffusion transformer that runs a shared group of transformer blocks several times within each denoising step, so the model gets deeper without getting larger. Deep supervision trains the prediction after every loop, and exclusive self-attention (XSA) regulates the attention updates inside the loop. The backbone is the pixel-space MMDiT of MiniT2I, conditioned on a frozen FLAN-T5-Large.

This repository holds the EMA weights of Looped-DiT B/32 at step 290k:

  • patch size 32, 512 x 512 images
  • [6,5,6] blocks (pre-loop, looped, post-loop), with the 5 looped blocks run 4 times
  • trained with deep supervision, with XSA in the looped blocks

Results

100 Euler steps, classifier-free guidance 6.0, loop depth 4. TIIF-Short is TIIF-Bench scored on its short prompts.

GenEvalDPG-BenchPRISMCoReBenchSpatialGenEvalTIIF-ShortAvg
85.185.354.444.552.376.166.3

Usage

Download the checkpoint, then sample with the Looped-DiT code (link coming soon):

hf download sensenova/Looped-DiT-B32 looped-dit-b32.pt --local-dir checkpoints
python -m looped_dit.sample --checkpoint checkpoints/looped-dit-b32.pt \
    --prompt "a red cube on top of a blue sphere" --out sample.png

Add --loops 1 2 3 4 to render the prompt at several loop depths. Other depths work without retraining.

item.title: SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT
item.content:encoded:
SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT

English | 简体中文

News

We introduce SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-TailSteer, extending SenseNova-U1.5 with substantially improved multi-turn editing stability while largely preserving its generation and editing capabilities.

Overview

SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT is our latest native unified multimodal checkpoint for more accurate, consistent, reliable, and aesthetically compelling visual creation. Built on NEO-unify, it strengthens the patchify layers, data quality and distribution, task formulation, prompt enhancement, and post-training pipeline.

The official release focuses on six user-visible improvements:

  • Higher-quality image generation: improved composition and color harmony, with more realistic material rendering, natural lighting, stronger visual fidelity, and finer local details.
  • Better text rendering and infographic generation: more legible Chinese and English text, with clearer information hierarchy in posters, infographics, brand assets, and other text-dense designs.
  • More efficient native 4K generation: more coherent global structure, color harmony, and stable high-resolution output with improved generation efficiency.
  • More reliable native image editing: stronger preservation of subject identity and unedited content across local, text, multi-reference, insertion, and replacement edits.
  • Stronger complex-instruction following: more consistent execution of object counts, spatial relationships, layouts, styles, and multiple constraints within a single request.
  • More precise visual control: more accurate region- and object-level control through bounding boxes, visual markers, and single- or multi-image references.

Showcases

Key Benchmarks

View detailed benchmark results

Quick Start

The reference inference implementation is available in the SenseNova-U1 GitHub repository.

Installation

git clone https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-U1.git
cd SenseNova-U1
uv sync
source .venv/bin/activate

The upstream environment uses Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.8, and CUDA 12.8. For other CUDA versions and optional FlashAttention configurations, see the installation guide.

Text-to-Image

python examples/t2i/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT \
  --prompt "A cinematic mountain lake at sunrise, realistic photography." \
  --width 2048 --height 2048 \
  --device_map auto \
  --output output.png

Image Editing

python examples/editing/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT \
  --image input.png \
  --prompt "Change the jacket to cobalt blue. Preserve the face, pose, background, lighting, and framing." \
  --output edited.png

See the inference examples for more options, supported resolutions, and batch processing.

Best Practices

Direct natural-language prompts work well for clear tasks with few constraints. For complex generation or editing, use prompt enhancement when additional planning is needed and explicitly specify what should remain unchanged.

See the SenseNova-U1.5 Cookbook for setup instructions and optional Image PE, Caption-to-Prompt, and Editing PE recipes.

🌐 Use with SenseNova-Studio

The fastest way to experience SenseNova-U1.5 is through SenseNova-Studio — a 🆓 free online playground where you can try the model directly in your browser, no installation or GPU required.

Ongoing Improvements

The official release improves upon the Preview, though challenges remain in:

  • Over-emphasized details or colors: some prompts may produce excessive high-frequency detail or oversaturated colors, which can often be mitigated by lowering cfg_scale.
  • Dense text errors: dense, lengthy, small, or mixed Chinese-English text may contain errors.
  • Constrained layouts: exact counts, alignment, or hierarchy may be imperfect in highly constrained layouts.
  • Unstable human details: small faces, hands, limbs, and fine-grained object structures may remain unstable.
  • Complex editing drift: broad, multi-turn, or multi-reference edits may drift, especially when many regions must be preserved simultaneously.

Models

ModelStageHF Weights
SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoTRL🤗 Model
SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-SFTSupervised fine-tuning🤗 Model
SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-TailSteerRL + TailSteer🤗 Model

🌐 Join the Community!

Join our growing community to share feedback, get support, and stay updated on the latest SenseNova-U1 developments — we'd love to hear from you!

DiscordFeishu Group

cd SenseNova-U1
uv sync
source .venv/bin/activate

The upstream environment uses Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.8, and CUDA 12.8. For other CUDA versions and optional FlashAttention configurations, see the installation guide.

Text-to-Image

python examples/t2i/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT \
  --prompt "A cinematic mountain lake at sunrise, realistic photography." \
  --width 2048 --height 2048 \
  --device_map auto \
  --output output.png

Image Editing

python examples/editing/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT \
  --image input.png \
  --prompt "Change the jacket to cobalt blue. Preserve the face, pose, background, lighting, and framing." \
  --output edited.png

See the inference examples for more options, supported resolutions, and batch processing.

Best Practices

Direct natural-language prompts work well for clear tasks with few constraints. For complex generation or editing, use prompt enhancement when additional planning is needed and explicitly specify what should remain unchanged.

See the SenseNova-U1.5 Cookbook for setup instructions and optional Image PE, Caption-to-Prompt, and Editing PE recipes.

🌐 Use with SenseNova-Studio

The fastest way to experience SenseNova-U1.5 is through SenseNova-Studio — a 🆓 free online playground where you can try the model directly in your browser, no installation or GPU required.

Ongoing Improvements

The official release improves upon the Preview, though challenges remain in:

  • Over-emphasized details or colors: some prompts may produce excessive high-frequency detail or oversaturated colors, which can often be mitigated by lowering cfg_scale.
  • Dense text errors: dense, lengthy, small, or mixed Chinese-English text may contain errors.
  • Constrained layouts: exact counts, alignment, or hierarchy may be imperfect in highly constrained layouts.
  • Unstable human details: small faces, hands, limbs, and fine-grained object structures may remain unstable.
  • Complex editing drift: broad, multi-turn, or multi-reference edits may drift, especially when many regions must be preserved simultaneously.

item.title: SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-Preview
item.content:encoded:
SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT (Preview)

English | 简体中文

NOTE: SenseNova-U1.5 (preview) offers an early look at our latest progress in image generation and editing. Notably, a more capable and refined production version will be officially released soon.

🌟 Overview

SenseNova-U1.5 (Preview) is a natively unified multimodal model built on NEO-unify, featuring new patch encoding and decoding layers. We further expand and refine the text-to-image training corpus, while extensively filtering and synthesizing editing data for both single-image and multi-image reference settings. Hence, it shows a notable leap in native image generation and editing:

  • Native 4K generation with remarkable efficiency, preserving both global coherence and fine-grained detail at high resolution.
  • Striking improvements in texture, material, lighting, and realism, producing richer and more visually convincing images.
  • Substantially stronger Chinese and English text rendering, together with more reliable composition of dense and complex layouts.
  • A major step forward in image editing, with stronger instruction following, subject-identity preservation, and structural consistency.
  • Fine-grained, region-controllable editing through masks, bounding boxes, and visual markers.

📣 Updated News

  • [2026.07.31] Released SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT (Preview), featuring native 4K generation, finer textures, complex layouts, and stronger editing capability. We also open-sourced the pre-training launcher and configuration.

Click to expand the SenseNova U1 updated history

  • [2026.07.16] Released SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V3 📊. The new version supports both infographic generation and editing. While retaining its infographic generation capabilities, it substantially improves local text, local content, global style, and global layout editing, including precise text correction in dense text. For model details and benchmark results, see ✨ U1 Infographic Model Series.
  • [2026.06.29] Released SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V2 📊. This version improves dense small-text rendering with sharper character edges, strengthens layout generation for complex and information-dense graphics, improves overall visual quality and coherence, and fixes the black-background issue. For model details and visual examples, see ✨ U1 Infographic Model Series.
  • [2026.06.12] Released SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-LoRA-8step-V1.0 for fast infographic generation. See the inference examples.
  • [2026.06.11] Released SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Interleaved 📖, optimized specifically for interleaved text-image generation. It substantially improves narrative coherence, character and style consistency, and text-image alignment across multi-page content such as picture books, storybooks, slide decks, and illustrated tutorials.
  • [2026.05.21] Released the full-parameter fine-tuning training code for SenseNova U1.
  • [2026.05.15] Released SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic 📊, improving infographic generation. For model details, see U1 Infographic Model Series; for 100 generation examples, see ✨ Infographic Showcases.
  • [2026.05.10] Released the 🔥 SenseNova U1 Technical Report 🔥 and open-sourced the SenseNova-U1-A3B-MoT-SFT and SenseNova-U1-A3B-MoT model weights.
  • [2026.05.08] Added GGUF quantized-weight support and a layered-loading VRAM mode for inference on a single GPU with limited memory. See the low-VRAM inference guide. GGUF weights for SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Merger are available at 🤗 smthem/SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Merger-gguf. We thank @smthem for contributing the quantized weights to the community.
  • [2026.05.06] Released SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-LoRA-8step-V1.0. See the inference examples.
  • [2026.04.30] Released the 8-step inference preview SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-8step-preview. In most cases, its image-generation quality is close to that of the base model. See the comparison and known issues. At runtime, follow the inference scripts and use --cfg_scale 1.0 --num_steps 8.
  • [2026.04.27] First released the SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-SFT and SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT model weights.
  • [2026.04.27] First released the SenseNova U1 inference code.

🔬 What U1.5 Improves

From Patchwise Prediction to Patch-Joint Reconstruction

SenseNova-U1's original MLP head reconstructs each RGB patch independently. At high resolutions, this can expose token boundaries as grid patterns, seams, or texture discontinuities. SenseNova-U1.5 instead adopts progressive spatial reconstruction via ConvDecoder: visual tokens are reshaped into a two-dimensional feature grid and upsampled through multiple Pixel Shuffle stages, with intermediate 3×3 convolutions enabling neighboring patches to interact and merge into a more continuous image.

Qualitative results show that this design substantially suppresses grid-like artifacts throughout pre-training. It also improves robustness during downstream adaptation, reducing the likelihood that similar artifacts re-emerge when fine-tuning on new domains.

From Instruction Following to Visual Preservation

SenseNova-U1 relied primarily on publicly available image-editing datasets, many of which contained noisy supervision, low-quality samples, and visible compositing or retouching artifacts. For SenseNova-U1.5, we extensively clean, filter, and synthesize the editing corpus, while improving Chinese–English balance and expanding coverage of both single-image and multi-image reference settings.

Quantitative results show that the encoder-free NEO-unify architecture achieves strong instruction following together with subject-identity and structural preservation using only a single sequence of reference-image tokens. This results in stronger editing performance and substantially higher inference efficiency, further validating the effectiveness of native unified multimodal modeling.

From Format Exposure to Cross-Task Generalization

The generation and editing corpora used to train SenseNova-U1.5 contain only a small number of simple JSON-formatted prompts, rather than long, hierarchical, or highly structured instructions. Besides, more complex JSON-like formats appear only in the understanding training data corpora, with substantially different content, structures and task objectives.

Despite this gap, it generalizes well to long and structured instructions in image generation and editing. This suggests that native unified multimodal modeling can combine capabilities learned from understanding and generation within a unified model, enabling structured comprehension and visual planning to transfer across tasks without dedicated training on fixed prompt templates.

✨ What U1.5 Achieves

🎨 Showcases

🖼️ Text-to-Image Showcase

The following examples cover several types of text-to-image tasks. Click a title in the left column to expand the complete original prompt.

PromptSenseNova-U1.5 (Preview)
Vintage soda advertisement 生成一张竖版复古可乐商业广告海报，品牌为“RETRO-COLA”，画面比例约为 2:3。整体采用 1960—1970 年代美式汽水广告、复古泳池派对摄影、旧杂志印刷和现代商业时尚广告融合的风格。画面必须真实、热烈、复古、富有生活方式气息，不能呈现为插画、卡通、漫画或明显的三维渲染。 场景设定在夏夜的户外露台或泳池派对。背景为深靛蓝色夜空，远处有少量暖黄色虚化灯光和轻微模糊的城市或派对环境。画面顶部撑开一把大型复古遮阳伞，伞面是奶油黄与焦糖橙相间的宽条纹，带真实布料褶皱、纤维质感和边缘流苏。遮阳伞占据画面顶部区域，但不能压住主要文字。 画面右侧中央是一位年轻女性，她是整张海报的人物主角。她有浓密蓬松的深棕色短卷发，佩戴金色圆环耳环、细项链和手镯，皮肤具有真实细腻的暖棕色质感。她表情自然、开怀大笑，充满夏夜派对的放松与感染力，像真实抓拍而不是僵硬摆拍。 她穿一件黄色与奶油白色格纹的复古修身连体泳装或复古吊带连衣装，胸口为复古收褶结构，肩带清楚，服装贴合身体但自然不过度夸张。人物采用稳定清晰的三分之四正面坐姿，稳定地坐在一个装满透明冰块的大型黄色金属冰桶里。上半身完整可见，头部、颈部、双肩、双臂和躯干结构清楚。她的背部自然挺直，肩膀放松，左右肩高度合理，胸腔和腰部略微朝向镜头，人体比例真实。 肢体结构必须清楚、简洁、稳定。画面中只保留主角自己的一双手，不要出现第三只手、额外手臂或从镜头外伸入的其他人的手。她的右手握住一瓶玻璃瓶装可乐，将瓶子自然举在胸口附近。右上臂贴近身体，手肘自然弯曲，前臂方向清楚。右手必须完整呈现五根手指，拇指在瓶身一侧，其余四指自然环绕瓶身，手指长度、关节和弯曲方向真实，不能粘连、穿模、扭曲，也不能遮挡主要标签文字。左手自然搭在黄色冰桶边缘，手掌放松，五根手指轻轻弯曲并清楚分开，手与桶沿有真实接触关系和轻微阴影，不隐藏在身体后方，也不与冰块、衣服或腿部融合。双臂不能交叉，双手不能遮挡脸部，也不能互相重叠。 腿部也要保持简洁稳定。人物只露出一条自然弯曲抬起的腿，只显示一个清楚的膝盖和部分大腿，膝盖位于画面中央偏右，形状自然，和躯干连接合理。另一条腿完全隐藏在冰桶和冰块内部，不要额外显示第二个膝盖、脚、小腿或重复腿部。冰桶边缘明确遮挡腰部以下位置，遮挡关系自然。不要采用双腿交叉、复杂盘腿、扭曲髋部或不可能的坐姿。 她右手拿着的可乐瓶必须保持真实产品结构：透明深棕色玻璃瓶、细长瓶颈、金属瓶盖、合理玻璃厚度和真实折射。瓶内装深褐色碳酸饮料，液面自然，内部有少量细密气泡，瓶外覆盖冷凝水珠。瓶身红棕色纸质标签上清晰显示品牌文字： “RETRO-COLA” 使用奶油白色复古粗衬线字体。标签紧贴瓶身曲面，不悬浮、不变形、不重复、不出现乱码。 画面底部中央是一只大型复古黄色金属冰桶，桶壁带真实冷凝水珠、少量磨损和金属反光。桶中堆满不规则透明冰块，冰块有自然裂纹、融水和高光。桶身正面印刷大型红棕色品牌文字： “DRINK” “RETRO-COLA” 其中“RETRO-COLA”使用复古弧形衬线字体，带少量星芒装饰，文字要清晰贴合桶体透视。 画面前景左右下角各放置一瓶靠近镜头的 RETRO-COLA 玻璃瓶。两瓶作为前景景深元素，被边缘轻微裁切，并略有前景虚化，但仍然能够辨认出深色玻璃、红棕标签和奶油白品牌文字。除了这两瓶前景产品，不要再加入额外人物手臂，不要有左下角伸手的动作元素。 画面左侧约占四成宽度，放置五行超大黄色英文标题： “VINTAGE” “CARBONATED” “DREAMS!” “UNCAP” “THE PAST.” 文字从上到下排列，使用高窄、极粗、略带手工印刷感的无衬线字体，颜色为芥末黄色。五行左对齐、行距紧凑、占据强烈视觉冲击力。标题位于人物左侧的深蓝夜空区域，不覆盖人物面部，不与可乐瓶标签重叠，每一行都必须清晰可读。 顶部中央放置较小黑色标题： “THE RETRO FIZZ®” 左上角放置三行黄色小字： “FUTURE” “RETRO” “FLAVOR” 右上角放置两行黄色小字： “RETRO-COLA” “LIFE 2026” 所有顶部小字均使用窄体粗无衬线字体，紧凑清晰，保持克制，不抢主体。 光线采用夜间派对中的暖色直接闪光灯或暖色商业布光与环境夜色结合。人物、玻璃瓶、冰块和黄色冰桶被温暖而清楚地照亮，皮肤、头发、玻璃瓶和冰块高光真实。背景保持深靛蓝色夜景和少量暖色散景。画面可以带适量复古胶片颗粒、轻微油墨噪点和旧杂志印刷感，但不能牺牲人物面部、手部、产品包装和文字清晰度。 整体配色以深靛蓝、芥末黄、焦糖橙、暖棕色、奶油白和可乐红棕色为主。整体气质像真实拍摄的复古汽水品牌广告，可用于饮料新品发布、夏季派对活动、电商主视觉和社交媒体营销。 特别强调： 主角只有一双手；右手握瓶，左手搭在冰桶边缘；只露出一个膝盖；另一条腿完全藏在冰桶中；不出现额外手臂、额外手指、重复膝盖、扭曲坐姿或肢体融合。

Typographic Form Editing 以基础图片进行局部文字造型编辑。仅将画面中央由海浪翻涌轨迹与白色船只共同拼出的巨大中文字符“迎”替换为“命”，目标字符必须清晰可识别为“命”。保持原图俯拍海面视角、青绿色海水、白色浪花、船只航行、飞鸟、顶部手写英文文字、底部白色中文文字、整体构图和画面比例不变。新的“命”字仍需由自然翻涌的白色海浪、泡沫水纹和船只航行轨迹组成，浪花边缘与原图质感一致，具有真实海面流动感，不要做成平面字体或贴图效果。将“命”字的最后一竖设计为原有白色船只的纵向航行形态，船只位置、透视、大小和光影尽量沿用原图，只调整周围浪花与水纹，使其自然成为“命”字结构的一部分。除“迎”改为“命”这一目标区域外，其他所有文字、海面纹理、飞鸟数量与位置、船只主体质感、色彩、光照、留白和整体旅行海报风格均保持不变。避免生成乱码、额外文字、错误汉字、重复船只、变形船体、突兀浪花、风格不一致或大范围重绘背景。
Region-Marked Editing 将红框内的文本“05月06日 10:00-17:00”替换为“06月18日 09:00-18:00”。保持原有的绿色字体、粗体样式和两行排版（第一行为日期，第二行为时间），并移除红框。

⚠️ Known Limitations

We aim to present SenseNova-U1.5 (Preview) with clear expectations. Its current limitations include:

  • Unintended text generation from short or underspecified prompts.
  • Errors in dense or lengthy text, especially for small characters and mixed Chinese-English content.
  • Incomplete adherence to complex layouts, including exact counts, alignment, and hierarchical structure.
  • Instability in small faces, hands, limbs, and fine-grained object details.
  • Drift in complex edits, particularly across broad, multi-turn, or multi-reference instructions.

To help users better reach the model’s current capability ceiling, we provide two optional open-source practices.

🧰 Best Practices [Strong Recommendation]

For tasks with a clear subject and few constraints, a direct natural-language prompt is sufficient. The two paths below are mainly intended for tasks where the design information is incomplete or where users want to re-create a mature visual solution from a reference. They are optional workflows external to the model and should not be conflated with the raw model's capabilities.

Path A: SenseNova Image PE Skill

Use this path when the input is only a short creative brief. The Skill turns the brief into a compact Render JSON prompt while preserving required subjects, visible copy, counts, layout constraints, and exclusions.

Installation

From the repository root, copy the Skill to the agent skills directory:

SKILL_DIR="$HOME/.agents/skills/sensenova-u1-5-prompt-enhancement"
mkdir -p "$SKILL_DIR"
cp src/sensenova_u1.5/prompt-enhancement-skill/SKILL.md "$SKILL_DIR/"
cp -R src/sensenova_u1.5/prompt-enhancement-skill/agents \
  src/sensenova_u1.5/prompt-enhancement-skill/references \
  "$SKILL_DIR/"

Usage Example

A Skill is a set of task instructions and references for an Agent, not a standalone program. After installation, invoke sensenova-u1-5-prompt-enhancement using your Agent's Skill mechanism and submit the request below. The Agent follows SKILL.md and the material in references/ to turn the brief into Render JSON. Invocation syntax varies by Agent. $SKILL_DIR is only the shell variable used by the installation command for the target directory.

Convert the brief below into one compact Render JSON object. Save only the JSON
object, without Markdown fences, to enhanced_prompt.json.

Brief:
Design a 3:4 portrait autumn lakeside wedding invitation with embossed paper
and delicate botanical linework. Use only this copy: "OUR DAY / AUTUMN WEDDING
/ 10.18 / LAKESIDE GARDEN".

Use the checked-in Render JSON to generate an image with SenseNova-U1.5:

MODEL_PATH="sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-Preview"

python examples/t2i/inference.py \
  --model_path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --prompt "$(cat src/sensenova_u1_5/prompt-enhancement-skill/examples/u1_5_pe_skill_wedding_prompt.json)" \
  --width 1760 \
  --height 2368 \
  --cfg_scale 4.0 \
  --cfg_norm global \
  --timestep_shift 3.0 \
  --num_steps 50 \
  --seed 1730675618 \
  --device_map auto \
  --output output.png

Path B: Reference-Image Retrieval + Caption-to-Prompt

When abstract style terms are not enough to describe a design target accurately, a more direct approach is to first retrieve a reference image with a high degree of design completeness, then use our Caption script to convert the visual decisions in that reference into an editable prompt:

Creative objective
  └─► Retrieve and select a reference image
      └─► SenseNova Caption Script
          └─► Composition / hierarchy / palette / typography / materials / lighting / constraints
              └─► Replace the theme, content, copy, subject, or local structure
                  └─► Re-create or reinterpret with SenseNova-U1.5

The key to this path is not simply copying a reference image, but decomposing why the design works into an executable description for the model. The Caption script attempts to extract the layout grid, visual focus, typographic hierarchy, color palette, materials, camera, lighting, and negative constraints. Users can then preserve the design language while replacing the theme, copy, subject, or local structure. When using external reference images, ensure that their source, authorization, and use comply with the applicable licenses.

Caption script: src/sensenova_u1_5/caption/caption.py

pip install openai pillow
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"

# Output a structured JSON prompt and a natural-language prompt
python src/sensenova_u1_5/caption/caption.py path/to/reference.jpg

# Save the result for subsequent changes to the theme, copy, subject, or local structure
python src/sensenova_u1_5/caption/caption.py path/to/reference.jpg > result.json

The following example uses the Caption script to produce a structured description, result.json, from the original reference image. It then uses that description for image reconstruction and for localized text and object edits.

OriginReversedV0V1

How to Choose

ScenarioRecommended Approach
Clear subject with few constraintsUse a direct natural-language prompt
Only a short creative brief is available, but a complete design plan should be filled in automaticallySenseNova Image PE Skill
An ideal composition or visual language has already been found and should be re-created, rethemed, or modifiedReference-image retrieval + Caption-to-Prompt

Editing PE

Editing PE is a prompt-preprocessing step for image editing and reference-guided generation. It sends the ordered input image(s) together with the original instruction to a multimodal prompt rewriter, which preserves the user's language and core intent while making the request more explicit for the image model. Depending on the task, it can clarify the edit target and location, assign roles to multiple reference images, extract a reference's visual language, specify exact text and layout, and state which subjects or regions must remain unchanged. The rewritten prompt is then passed to SenseNova-U1.5 for image generation; Editing PE does not modify pixels itself.

The standalone implementation is available at src/sensenova_u1_5/edit/edit_pe.py. To inspect the rewritten prompt without starting image generation:

export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
# Optional:
# export OPENAI_MODEL="gpt-5.5"
# export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://your-openai-compatible-endpoint/v1"

python src/sensenova_u1_5/edit/edit_pe.py \
  path/to/input.png \
  "把天空改成晚霞"

The command prints the rewritten prompt to standard output. Multiple input images can be listed in order before the original prompt.

In examples/editing/inference.py, Editing PE is disabled by default. Enable it with --use-edit-pe and set OPENAI_API_KEY. Use --print-edit-pe to inspect the original and rewritten prompts, or --edit-pe-model to select the rewriter model. For multi-image tasks, provide the images in the intended order and describe each image's role in the original instruction.

The following example shows how a short style-reference request is expanded into a detailed, model-facing instruction, and compares the outputs before and after enhancement.

Input ImageOriginal PromptOriginal Prompt OutputPE-Enhanced PromptPE-Enhanced Prompt Output
参考这张图的青花水墨视觉语言，生成一张中国古建筑屋顶形制图鉴。View full PE-enhanced prompt 参考输入图的青花瓷与水墨视觉语言，生成一张竖版《中国古建筑屋顶形制图鉴》信息海报。整体使用白色宣纸背景、淡灰水墨山水远景、青花蓝单色主调、细腻瓷纹边框、传统卷草纹与云纹装饰，版式层级、圆形插图框、编号徽章、虚线分隔和说明卡片风格与参考图一致，但内容改为中国古建筑屋顶形制。 左侧设置大号竖排书法标题文字“屋顶形制”，使用深青蓝粗笔触。标题旁加入竖排副标题“飞檐斗拱之间，承载千年营造智慧”。左下角绘制一座青花瓷质感的古建筑屋脊与飞檐局部，带有花纹装饰和水墨阴影，替代参考图中的茶碗。背景保留淡雅山水、竹叶、云纹和留白感。 右侧从上到下排列 6 个屋顶形制条目，每个条目包含一个圆形青花瓷边框插图，里面用蓝灰线描绘对应屋顶轮廓；右侧连接一张青花边框信息卡。每张卡片包含编号、屋顶名称、简短特征和代表建筑，文字清晰可读，全部使用深青蓝色。 6 个条目的文字内容如下： “庑殿顶” “等级：最高” “特征：四坡五脊，庄重宏阔” “代表：太和殿” “歇山顶” “等级：高” “特征：九脊结合，山花分明” “代表：故宫保和殿” “悬山顶” “等级：中” “特征：两坡出山墙，屋檩外挑” “代表：民居祠堂” “硬山顶” “等级：常见” “特征：两坡封山墙，朴素稳重” “代表：北方民居” “攒尖顶” “等级：亭阁常用” “特征：多坡汇于一点，形制挺拔” “代表：天坛祈年殿” “卷棚顶” “等级：园林常用” “特征：无正脊，曲线柔和” “代表：园林廊亭” 保持整张海报为精致青花水墨插画风，避免现代图标和鲜艳颜色。构图清爽、对齐整齐、装饰细节丰富但不影响文字阅读。

🚀 Quick Start

The reference inference implementation is available in the SenseNova-U1 GitHub repository.

Installation

git clone https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-U1.git
cd SenseNova-U1
uv sync
source .venv/bin/activate

The upstream environment currently uses Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.8, and CUDA 12.8. For other CUDA versions and optional FlashAttention configurations, see the installation guide.

🖼️ Text-to-Image

python examples/t2i/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-Preview \
  --prompt "A cinematic mountain lake at sunrise, realistic photography." \
  --width 2048 --height 2048 \
  --device_map auto \
  --output output.png

✏️ Image Editing

python examples/editing/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-Preview \
  --image input.png \
  --prompt "Change the jacket to cobalt blue. Preserve the face, pose, background, lighting, and framing." \
  --output edited.png

To use Image PE to generate a more detailed model-facing editing prompt:

python examples/editing/inference.py \
  --model_path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT-Preview \
  --prompt "参考这张图的青花水墨视觉语言，生成一张中国古建筑屋顶形制图鉴。" \
  --image docs/assets/showcases/editing_gallery/case1_ancient_roof_infographic.webp \
  --output edited_with_pe.png \
  --use-edit-pe

The reference configuration for SenseNova-U1.5 is cfg_scale=4.0, timestep_shift=3.0, and num_steps=50.

Training

The SenseNova-U1.5 generation pre-training code is available in the training directory. After configuring the model, tokenizer, and data paths, launch the provided pixel-head PT recipe with:

cd training
bash shell/train_u1/U1.5_8B.sh

The environment-driven PT configuration is sensenovau1_5_8b_mot_pt.py.

🌐 Join the Community!

Join our growing community to share feedback, get support, and stay updated on the latest SenseNova-U1 developments — we'd love to hear from you!

item.title: SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V3
item.content:encoded:
SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V3

English | 简体中文

📣 Updated News

  • [2026.07.16] Release SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V3 📊, designed for integrated infographic generation and editing. It retains strong text-to-image (T2I) capabilities while significantly enhancing infographic editing, supporting localized text and content editing, global style editing, and global layout editing. See ✨ U1 Infographic Model Series for model details and benchmark results.

✨ Click to expand older news

  • [2026.06.29] Release SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V2 📊, an upgraded infographic model with improved dense small-text rendering with sharper text edges, stronger complex dense-layout generation, and better overall visual aesthetics and harmony, plus a fix for the black-background issue. Model details and visual examples are available in ✨ U1 Infographic Model Series.
  • [2026.06.12] Release SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-LoRA-8step-V1.0 for faster infographic generation. Please see the example script.
  • [2026.06.11] Release SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Interleaved 📖, specially optimized for interleaved image-text generation, with notably improved narrative coherence, character and style consistency, and text-image alignment in multi-page content.
  • [2026.05.21] Release the full-parameter fine-tuning training code for SenseNova-U1.
  • [2026.05.15] Release SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic 📊 model for improved infographic generation. See U1 Infographic Model Series for details, and ✨ Infographic Showcases for 100 generated examples.
  • [2026.05.10] Release 🔥SenseNova-U1 Technical Report🔥 and the weights for SenseNova-U1-A3B-MoT-SFT & SenseNova-U1-A3B-MoT.
  • [2026.05.08] Add GGUF quantized checkpoints and layer-offload VRAM modes for low-VRAM single-GPU inference. See Memory-efficient inference. GGUF weights for SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Merger are available at 🤗 smthem/SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Merger-gguf — many thanks to @smthem for contributing the quantized weights.
  • [2026.05.06] Release SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-LoRA-8step-V1.0. Please see the example script.
  • [2026.04.30] Release the preview version of the 8-step inference model SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-8step-preview. In most cases, the image generation quality of this model closely matches that of the base model (see comparison and existing issues). To test this model, you can use the inference scripts, but with the following parameters: --cfg_scale 1.0 --num_steps 8 .
  • [2026.04.27] Initial release of the weights for SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-SFT and SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT.
  • [2026.04.27] Initial release of the inference code for SenseNova-U1.

🌟 Overview

🚀 SenseNova U1 is a new series of native multimodal models that unifies multimodal understanding, reasoning, and generation within a monolithic architecture. It marks a fundamental paradigm shift in multimodal AI: from modality integration to true unification. Rather than relying on adapters to translate between modalities, SenseNova U1 models think-and-act across language and vision natively.

✨ Click to expand architecture details

Unifying visual understanding and generation in an end-to-end architecture from pixel to word opens tremendous possibilities, enabling highly efficient and strong understanding, generation, and interleaved reasoning in a natively multimodal manner.

🏗️ Key Pillars:

At the core of SenseNova U1 is NEO-unify, a novel architecture designed from the first principles for multimodal AI: It eliminates both Visual Encoder (VE) and Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) where pixel-word information are inherently and deeply correlated. Several important features are as follows:

  • 🔗 Model language and visual information end-to-end as a unified compound.
  • 🖼️ Preserve semantic richness while maintaining pixel-level visual fidelity.
  • 🧠 Reason across modalities with high efficiency & minimal conflict via native MoTs.

Powered by this new core architecture, SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V3 is the recommended release for an integrated infographic generation-and-editing workflow. It retains strong text-to-image (T2I) capability while adding image editing (IT2I) within the same unified model.

  • Benchmark Performance: V3 reaches an Overall Total of 50.23 on Qwen-Image-Bench, improving by 2.23 over V2's 48.00. It also achieves an Average of 5.89 on WeEdit and an overall score of 7.89 on GEdit-Bench, ranking first among the open-source models included in both editing evaluations.
  • Generation and Editing Quality: V3 supports both region-marked precise changes and natural-language-only editing. It handles localized text edits, local content insertion, removal, and replacement, as well as global style and layout editing, while preserving unedited regions whenever possible.

IGenBench scores are reported as percentages; the remaining commercial and open-source models are sorted separately by the average of BizGenEval hard/easy and IGenBench Q-ACC/I-ACC. OneIG is included as a general generation reference.

V2 and V3 are independently trained from the same base model with different task and data mixtures. V3 jointly trains infographic text-to-image generation and image editing with a lower proportion of IGenBench-related training data than V2, resulting in lower IGenBench scores than the generation-focused V2. At the same time, V3 remains broadly comparable to V2 on BizGenEval, improves the broader Qwen-Image-Bench score from 48.00 to 50.23, and adds infographic image-editing capability.

SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V3 Showcase

The following V3 examples are organized around integrated infographic generation-and-editing capabilities. They cover T2I generation and IT2I editing scenarios, including four major editing capability groups: local text editing, local content editing, global style editing, and global layout editing, and demonstrate precise dense-text repair and consistency preservation in non-edited regions.

Local Text Editing

Region-Marked Precise Editing

InstructionBefore EditAfter Edit
Instruction将蓝色框中的屋顶变为红色，将红框中的标题改为比较简短的格式，将绿框中的屋子改为红色屋顶的咖啡屋，将紫色框中改为共享自行车站，将粉色框中的内容改为书柜，将右下角青色框中的内容改为，室内植物玻璃房

Instruction请在图像中红色边界框标出的空白区域内插入指定内容，并使新增内容与真实环境的材质、透视、光照和空间关系自然融合。 目标区域： “画面左下角主面板下方的空白深色区域，位于左侧四个数据卡片下方、底部图表左侧的红色边界框内部” 需要插入的文字或内容为： “年度结余目标：120,000元” 请严格将新增内容限制在红框内部。完成插入后，需要彻底去除红色边界框，使最终图像中不再显示任何红线、控制点、箭头或编辑标记。 在插入内容之前，请先分析目标区域的实际环境，包括： 深色金融仪表盘背景的平面方向； 目标区域的矩形仪表盘面板边界； 玻璃拟态卡片、深色渐变背景和细线边框材质； 光源方向和亮度； 环境阴影与微弱高光； 字体应该像金融仪表盘中的数字标签和状态卡片，而不是普通贴纸文字。 新增文字必须按照目标表面的透视自然放置。由于目标区域是正面仪表盘平面，文字应保持水平排版、居中或左对齐，并与原有卡片网格对齐。 新增内容的颜色、亮度和清晰度必须符合环境光照。建议使用浅色文字配合绿色或金色强调数字，使其与原图“储蓄率 41%”“目标完成 76%”等数据卡片风格一致。不能使用与场景完全无关的纯白贴字，也不能让文字看起来悬浮在表面前方。 如果目标区域是仪表盘卡片： 文字应在红框内部合理居中； 保留原有深色面板边缘、微弱发光和阴影； 不得覆盖相邻卡片、图表或边框； 可以根据原有设计加入适当内边距和小型图标。 插入的文字必须完整、清晰、无乱码、无错别字。字体风格应与金融仪表盘和数据卡片用途相符，不得使用与场景冲突的字体。 除红框内部区域和红框本身之外，图像中的其他内容必须保持完全不变。不得移动标题“个人年度财务仪表盘”、左侧数据卡、现金流图、储蓄仪表、支出分类图、目标追踪列表或任何其他物体，不得改变整体光照、颜色和构图。 不得扩大目标区域，不得把新增内容放到红框外，也不得保留红框作为最终设计元素。 最重要的是，新增内容必须像原本就存在于该金融仪表盘中，而不是后来粘贴上去。最终画面应具有正确的材质融合、环境光照、卡片层级和自然对齐关系。
Instruction将原西班牙语标题替换为英文“STOP USING SHOWER SPONGES!”和副标题“YOUR SKIN DESERVES BETTER”，移除红框，框外所有文字、人物、颜色和布局完全不变。
